Other Income Sources
The federal Government could exchange federal coal from another location for that on new or proposed Crow coal lease areas. The exchange would serve to transfer the environmental impacts as described in Chapter III to another location, since other coal used as a substitute for the Crow coal will have similiar impacts but at different areas. This would be a multi-level trade-off affecting Indians and non-Indians.
The federal Government could also purchase the coal outright from the Crow Indians if new leasing is rejected. While there are no accurate estimates of the total amount of funding needed for such a buy-out, the huge tonnages of coal reserves indicate that the figure would be large. This alternative might require new legislation if it were seriously considered. The federal Government may elect to mine this purchased coal at a future date. If this were to take place the environmental impacts previously discussed would occur.
Additional income to the Tribe and to the tribal members could also be provided through federal grants and welfare assistance. These sources have been providing a substantial portion of the income to the Crow people over the past several years. In fact, increased need for these income sources can be expected unless development of Crow Indian coal resources takes place.
Environmental impacts under these income alternatives would be the same as for the no development alternative, except that the Crow Indians would receive income benefits.
